ratios.analogy: An octave is a 2:1 frequency ratio and a perfect fifth is 3:2.
ratios.worked_example: A string at 220 Hz sounds an octave above at 440 Hz.
ratios.why_valid: Pitch intervals are defined by frequency ratios.
ratios.limits: Only covers ratio intuition, not ratio word problems.

fractions.analogy: Musical time signatures and notes (whole, half, quarter, eighth) represent fractional divisions of a measure.
fractions.worked_example: Two half notes or four quarter notes equal one whole note (1/2 + 1/2 = 1).
fractions.why_valid: Rhythm and meter are exact fractional divisions.
fractions.limits: Does not explain non-standard fraction arithmetic.

limits.reason: No sound analogy that is mathematically accurate.

probability.analogy: Loot drop rates and critical strike chances are calculated using event probabilities.
probability.worked_example: A 5% critical strike chance means an expected 1 in 20 hits.
probability.why_valid: Game mechanics directly employ RNG probability distributions.
probability.limits: Pseudo-random distribution algorithms may alter raw odds in games.

angles.analogy: Passing and shooting trajectories in soccer or basketball depend directly on launch angle.
angles.why_valid: Kinematic vector physics defines flight paths.
angles.limits: Wind and spin deflect real ball flights.
